summary.en: Map a large key space into a small array and compare three ways to calculate a bucket.
summary.bn: বড় কী থেকে ছোট অ্যারের ইনডেক্স বানিয়ে তিন ধরনের হ্যাশ ফাংশন দেখো।

notes: C17 defines integer remainder with the sign of the dividend, so normalize negative results before indexing. The multiplication example requires the optional exact-width uint32_t and uint64_t types. Its numeric string-hash discussion assumes ASCII-compatible character codes.

sections.title: Turn a key into an array position
Three ways to calculate a bucket
Watch the mapping before storing records
Judge a hash against actual keys
Do not confuse a hash with an identity
Use the index as a starting point

examples.title: Division hashing and negative keys
examples.explanationHtml: 22 and 33 share bucket zero; -1 and 10 share bucket ten. Three distinct buckets hold five keys.

examples.title: A 32-bit multiplication hash
examples.explanationHtml: The low 32 product bits represent a fractional position. Taking its top four bits selects one of sixteen buckets.

examples.title: A rolling hash for a word
examples.explanationHtml: Each byte contributes after the previous hash is multiplied by 31. The running remainder keeps multiplication small.

practice.title: Count shared division buckets
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..12) and n int keys. Print Count and keys:, each key as K -> B using modulus 11, then collisions=C. Count every key after the first in its bucket, including equal keys.

practice.title: Hash a contact name
practice.statementHtml: Read one word of 1..24 non-space bytes. Print Word (1..24 non-space characters): then hash=H using h=(31*h+byte)%101, starting at zero.

practice.title: Reserve cells or hash keys?
practice.statementHtml: Student IDs range from 0 to 999999, but only 2000 IDs are stored. Compare direct addressing and 4001 hash buckets.
hints: Separate possible IDs from stored IDs.
practice.answerHtml: Direct addressing needs 1000000 cells and handles IDs without collisions. Hashing uses 4001 bucket headers plus records; its load factor is 2000/4001, about 0.5. Distinct IDs may share a bucket, so equality still needs checking.

practice.title: Bad last-digit hashing
practice.statementHtml: Explain why key%10 performs badly for IDs 120,230,340,450, even though ten buckets exist.
practice.answerHtml: All four IDs end in zero, so every key maps to bucket zero. Nine cells remain unused. Changing the modulus can help this pattern, but no modulus prevents every possible collision. Inspect representative IDs before choosing a function.

quiz.prompt: When IDs can take a million values but only a thousand are stored, what wastes direct-address space?
options: A cell is reserved for every possible ID
Only used IDs need cells
Collisions allocate extra ID ranges
Each ID needs a linked list
quiz.explanation: Direct addressing indexes the entire universe, including unused IDs.

quiz.prompt: Can two unequal keys produce the same bucket index?
options: No, if keys are positive
Yes, when their hashes collide
No, if capacity is prime
Only if the keys are strings
quiz.explanation: A smaller bucket space cannot uniquely represent every key in a larger universe.

quiz.prompt: Which property is necessary for repeatable dictionary lookup?
options: Every key must map to zero
Capacity must always equal key count
Equal keys must map identically under the same hash settings
Hashing must change on each call
quiz.explanation: Search must reproduce insertion placement before comparing candidate keys.

quiz.prompt: Why does a rolling string hash multiply the previous value?
options: To prevent every possible collision
To sort the characters
To avoid reading the string
To make character positions affect the result
quiz.explanation: A plain sum ignores order, while rolling accumulation preserves some positional information.

quiz.prompt: What is the cost of hashing a string of L bytes with the rolling loop?
options: O(L) time and O(1) working space
O(1) time regardless of L
O(L squared) time
O(L) extra array space
quiz.explanation: The loop inspects each byte once and retains only a running remainder.

quiz.prompt: Which key pattern is a poor match for key%10?
options: Keys evenly using all final digits
Keys that all end in zero
Keys from zero through nine
Any ten distinct consecutive nonnegative keys
quiz.explanation: All trailing-zero keys collide even when other buckets remain unused.

quiz.prompt: Why does the multiplication example use unsigned fixed-width arithmetic?
options: Signed overflow produces better hashes
It makes the table collision-free
It defines the retained 32-bit product before extracting four index bits
It removes the need to store original keys
quiz.explanation: The fixed-width word represents a fractional product; it does not establish key identity.

quiz.prompt: How does the normalized modulus map -1 into eleven buckets?
quiz.explanation: Normalization adds the positive modulus to a negative remainder.

quiz.prompt: How many extra arrivals collide when 1,12,23 share a bucket?
quiz.explanation: The first arrival uses the bucket; two later arrivals collide.

quiz.prompt: Which rolling remainder follows two numeric bytes 2 and 3?

keyPoints.en: Direct addressing reserves a cell for every possible key.
keyPoints.bn: ডাইরেক্ট অ্যাড্রেসিংয়ে প্রতিটা সম্ভাব্য কীয়ের জন্য একটা সেল লাগে।

keyPoints.en: Hashing trades unused cells for possible collisions.
keyPoints.bn: হ্যাশিংয়ে কম সেল লাগে, তবে এক ইনডেক্সে একাধিক কী আসতে পারে।

keyPoints.en: Normalize a negative remainder before indexing an array.
keyPoints.bn: নেগেটিভ ভাগশেষ ঠিক করে তারপর অ্যারের ইনডেক্স হিসেবে নাও।

keyPoints.en: A string hash must process every character in order.
keyPoints.bn: স্ট্রিং হ্যাশে প্রতিটা অক্ষর ক্রম ধরে হিসাব করতে হয়।

keyPoints.en: A good distribution depends on the keys you expect.
keyPoints.bn: কী কেমন হবে, তার ওপর ভালো হ্যাশ ফাংশন বেছে নেওয়া নির্ভর করে।

22 33 -1 10 7. Show the intermediate memory or worklist changes.
